query_snapshot: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- The archived NIOSH table lists Butyl, Teflon, Saranex, Barricade, Responder, Trellchem, and Tychem in the 8-hour protective-clothing group for hydrogen chloride. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The archived NIOSH table lists Neoprene and PVC in the 4-hour protective-clothing group for hydrogen chloride. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry in the archived NIOSH table includes the hazard phrase "Prevent skin contact (solution)." [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry in the archived NIOSH table includes the hazard word "Frostbite." [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry in the archived NIOSH table includes the note "Prevent possible skin freezing from direct liquid contact." [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
